nc_sentinel_buttress_boulderfield.blurb: Sentinel Buttress Boulderfield is one of the boulder fields at Moore's Wall in Hanging Rock State Park, in North Carolina's Piedmont. Nearly every climb is a boulder problem, spread fairly evenly from V0 up to about V8, with a couple of harder ones beyond. The Central Area holds most of the problems, among many huge boulders and a number of smaller ones, and was an early development site. Trailside Boulderfield holds a smaller group. Tree cover gives the boulders good shade.

ut_brian_head.blurb: Brian Head is a high mountain climbing area around the resort town of the same name in southwest Utah, with its crags found along Highway 143 near Cedar Breaks. The town sits near 9,600 feet, and the climbing is practical only for a short stretch of summer and early fall, when temperatures rarely pass about 75 degrees F, though thunderstorms can build quickly and mornings and evenings stay cold. Bouldering and sport are about equal, with a little trad. Sport routes run from 5.7 to 5.13, mostly 5.9 to 5.11, at The Overlook, Running Scared Wall and The Principality, while Bunker Creek holds the boulder problems, mostly V0 to V6.

al_bishop_mountain.blurb: Bishop Mountain is a bouldering area near Huntsville, Alabama, and every problem on it is a boulder problem. Grades run from V0 up to V11, with the bulk between V1 and V6 and a handful of harder lines above. At Middle Bishop the boulders sit in woods on a hillside, and walks from the road take roughly two to fifteen minutes. Middle Bishop is the main cluster and holds most of the established problems, while Right Bishop and Left Bishop have far fewer. Omen Area and Shelf Life Area are small additions with only a few problems each.

nm_enchanted_tower.blurb: Enchanted Tower is a sport climbing area near Datil, New Mexico, in the Datil Range, at roughly 7,900 feet. It sits in a larger valley with several crags along its walls, running roughly east to west from The Giants Molars and Frog Prince to The Land Beyond. Nearly everything is sport, mostly 5.10 to 5.12 with a handful of 5.13s and a few easier lines. Rapunzel Wall and Mother Goose Wall are the beginner-friendly ones. The Enchanted Tower itself is a free-standing wedge of usually overhanging rock with hard routes, its North Face typically shaded and its West Face typically sunny.
